nodes.notes: POST { "access_token": "<user's JWT access token>" }. The workflow acts as that user — Django's own auth/ownership checks still apply, so this can never touch another user's resume.

nodes.name: Trigger Resume Analysis (Django)
nodes.notes: Calls Django's existing POST /api/analysis/analyze/ — the exact same endpoint the React frontend calls. Django internally calls the FastAPI AI service for the Gemini part. This node duplicates none of that logic; it only sequences an HTTP call.

meta.description: Optional orchestration entry point for the existing resume analysis pipeline (Module 3). Resume upload, PDF extraction (Module 2), and RAG chunking/embedding/indexing (Module 4) already happen automatically inside Django the moment a resume finishes processing — this workflow does not re-implement or replace any of that. It exists so an external trigger (an admin tool, a scheduled re-analysis, a support script) can kick off analysis for a given user by calling Django's own authenticated API, the same way the React frontend does, without n8n needing to know anything about Gemini, chunking, or ChromaDB.
